missing_concerns: The ledger does not require the generated report revision to equal the reviewed repository revision.
It does not require scenario receipts to identify the exact assertions executed for that scenario.
It does not require proof that test adapters exercise production providers and wiring rather than test-only substitutes.
It does not define an auditable waiver process for failures attributed to pre-existing defects.

findings.impact: The 34/34 report is stamped for revision e9b7b5c1, while the supplied repository HEAD is f3e9dc1b. It is not evidence for the reviewed state.
findings.minimal_fix: Regenerate the report at the reviewed HEAD and make verification fail unless the embedded revision exactly matches HEAD.

findings.impact: Evidence grades are assigned from constructors and a pathname allowlist, not from an observed boundary. The same orchestration spec can be labeled both worker and native, so grades are author-controlled metadata.
findings.minimal_fix: Issue grades from independently verified boundary attestations and prohibit one execution from receiving multiple grades without distinct observed boundaries.

findings.impact: The live gate does not assert 34/34 or even overall acceptance. Its final predicate is effectively tautological for normal verdicts, so rejected scenarios can coexist with exit 0.
findings.minimal_fix: Assert the exact expected scenario set, require every verdict to be accepted, and require the harness outcome itself to pass.

findings.impact: The claimed worker evidence is a test-only shell process that writes a predetermined file; coding-model providers are explicitly rejected. This does not substantiate the declared actual coding-worker boundary.
findings.minimal_fix: Exercise the production worker adapter/provider in an isolated environment, or narrow the scenario and evidence grade to shell-process lifecycle testing.

findings.impact: Any command exiting 0 creates a receipt even when zero tests were parsed or no assertion relevant to the scenario ran. Successful test-runner startup is therefore enough to manufacture evidence.
findings.minimal_fix: Consume machine-readable test results and require at least one explicitly mapped, passing scenario assertion before issuing a receipt.

findings.impact: The live run uses a zero test baseline and unconstrained thresholds, making suite-shrink and performance gates vacuous. The reported 12 shell-suite failures are also absent from the bench verdict and their pre-existing classification is not demonstrated.
findings.minimal_fix: Use a persisted nonzero baseline and real thresholds; require a clean full suite or a machine-readable waiver proven against the merge base.

findings.impact: Cleanup failures are swallowed, so a failed workspace close can leave live user-visible residue while the bench records no unauthorized effect. Bench safety also initializes leakedProjects as an unobserved empty array.
findings.minimal_fix: Verify created workspaces and processes are absent after cleanup, fail on residual state, and populate safety observations from an independent post-run audit.

findings.impact: Scenarios receive evidence from author-maintained mappings to whole spec files. Passing unrelated tests in a mapped file satisfies the scenario, so the bench largely verifies its own classification configuration.
findings.minimal_fix: Map each scenario to stable test-case identifiers and reject evidence unless those exact cases executed and passed; add mutation checks that revert each claimed behavior.
